rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a report in Muslim’s Ṣaḥīḥ that whoever enumerates God’s ninety-nine names enters Paradise; it describes God as One who loves oddness.
rows.anchor: إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا من أحصاها دخل الجنة إنه وتر يحب الوتر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: The idolaters deviated from God’s names by deriving al-Lāt from Allah, al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, and Manāt from al-Mannān.
rows.anchor: فاشتقوا اللات من الله والعزى من العزيز ومنات من المنان عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broader interpretation is that they attribute to God descriptions or names that do not befit Him or may not be used for Him.
rows.anchor: إن معنى يلحدون في أسمائه يصفونه بما لا يليق به ويسمونه بما لا يجوز تسميته به

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī includes calling Jesus God’s son among the forbidden ways of naming God; the author says this broader reading has wider benefit.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه أعم فائدة ويدخل فيه قول الجبائي أراد تسميتهم المسيح بأنه ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that God may be named only by the names He has applied to Himself.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه لا يجوز أن يسمى الله تعالى إلا بما سمى به نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat of recompense applies in the Hereafter; another view extends it to this world and the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة. وقيل: في الدنيا والآخرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says that a group among His creation guides people to His true religion and judges by the truth.
rows.anchor: جماعة وعصبة يدعون الناس إلى توحيد الله تعالى وإلى دينه وهو الحق يرشدونهم إليه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports the Prophet saying that his community has people who take and give by the truth, like a comparable group before them among Moses’s people.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" هي لأمتي بالحق يأخذون وبالحق يعطون

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas reports the Prophet reciting the verse and saying that people in his community will uphold truth until Jesus descends.
rows.anchor:
وقال الربيع بن أنس: قرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية فقال:
" إن من أمتي قوما على الحق حتى ينزل عيسى ابن مريم "

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين علي
rows.claim: In a report transmitted by al-ʿAyyāshī, ʿAlī says the community will divide into seventy-three sects, all destined for Fire except the single group described here.
rows.anchor: عن أمير المؤمنين علي ع أنه قال: والذي نفسي بيده لتفترقن هذه الأمة على ثلاث وسبعين فرقة كلها في النار

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd Allāh identify themselves as the group that guides and judges by truth.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله ع أنهما قالا نحن هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One coherence reading contrasts the preceding account of heedless unbelievers with the people who guide to truth and judge justly.
rows.anchor: لما بين في الآية المتقدمة حال قوم من الكفار يغفلون عن الحق بين في هذه الآية أن من جملة ما خلق من يهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the passage connects to the earlier phrase ذرأنا and contrasts two groups created with different qualities.
rows.anchor: أنه يتصل بقوله ذرأنا فكأنه قال خلقنا قوما صفتهم كذا وكذا وقوما صفتهم كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʾb means a habitual custom or way; the word can describe continuing an action as one’s regular practice.
rows.anchor: الدأب العادة والطريقة يقال ما زال ذلك دأبه ودينه وديدنه

rows.speaker: خداش بن زهير
rows.claim: Khudāsh ibn Zuhayr’s verse uses dāʾb for a continuing customary course of action.
rows.anchor: وما زال ذاك الدأب حتى تخاذلت هوازن وارفضت سليم وعامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing something means making it other than its former state in a way that would be evident if it were observed.
rows.anchor: والتغيير تصيير الشيء على خلاف ما كان بما لو شوهد على خلاف ما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ka-daʾbi, the comparison phrase is the nominative predicate, though its wording is accusative under an understood verb, as in Zayd is behind you.
rows.anchor: الكاف في موضع رفع بأنه خبر المبتدأ كما يقول زيد خلفك فموضع خلفك رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam yak is shortened from yakūn: jussive mood drops its wāw, then frequent use permits dropping the nūn without obscuring meaning.
rows.anchor: لم يك أصله يكون فحذفت الواو للجزم ثم حذفت النون استخفافا لكثرة الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna is the mother of verbs because its meanings are implicit in other verbs; its strength and frequent use permit deletion unlike forms such as lam yaṣun.
rows.anchor: لأن كان ويكون أم الأفعال ألا ترى أن كل فعل فيه معناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ pattern of rejecting Muḥammad resembles Pharaoh’s people and earlier nations in rejecting messengers and revelation.
rows.anchor: عادة هؤلاء المشركين في الكفر بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم كعادة آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the comparison to mean that God’s punishment of these disbelievers matched His punishment of Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: معناه عقوبة الله تعالى لهؤلاء الكفار كعقوبة لآل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āl Firʿawn denotes Pharaoh’s followers, while aṣḥāb Firʿawn is based on companionship and commonly denotes shared affiliation; āl usually indicates close lineage.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين آل فرعون وأصحاب فرعون أن الأصحاب مأخوذ من الصحبة وكثر في الموافقة في المذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seized them for their sins; He is powerful, with no one able to prevent the punishment He chooses to impose.
rows.anchor: أي قادر لا يقدر أحد على منعه عن إحلال العقاب بما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description severe applies to punishment, not to God Himself, because shadīd literally suggests something tightly interlocked and difficult to separate.
rows.anchor: ولا يوصف الله سبحانه بأنه شديد لأن الشديد هو المتداخل على صعوبة تفككه وإنما وصف العقاب بالشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ destruction was hastened as Pharaoh’s people received an immediate, comprehensive punishment.
rows.anchor: تعجيل العقاب لهؤلاء بالإهلاك كتعجيله لأولئك بعذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not remove a blessing until a people change from a praiseworthy state to a blameworthy one, replacing obedience with sin and gratitude with ingratitude.
rows.anchor: حتى يتغيروا هم عن أحوالهم المرضية إلى أحوال لا يجوز لهم أن يتغيروا إليها وهو أن يستبدلوا المعصية بالطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may withdraw a blessing as a beneficial test, but removes it as punishment only from those who deserve punishment.
rows.anchor: وقد يسلب الله تعالى النعمة على وجه المصلحة لا على وجه العقاب امتحانا لمصلحة يعلمها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the blessing was Muḥammad, whom God gave to Quraysh; after they rejected him, He transferred him to the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: النعمة التي أنعمها الله عليهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أنعم الله به على قريش فكفروا به وكذبوه فنقله إلى الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what people say and knows their innermost thoughts and everything.
rows.anchor: { وأن الله سميع } لأقوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated comparison again calls the disbelievers’ way their habitual practice of denying God’s signs.
rows.anchor: أي كعادتهم وطريقتهم في التكذيب بآيات الله عادة هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial was of their Lord’s proofs and clear evidences, and God made them perish for their sins, drowning Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: وبيناته { فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم } أي استأصلناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the destroyed groups wronged themselves, so each was punished only after deserving it.
rows.anchor: كل هولاء المهلكين كانوا ظالمين لأنفسهم فلم نعاقب فريقا منهم إلا عن استحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the first comparison establishes their deserving punishment in the Hereafter, while the repetition establishes their deserving worldly punishment.
rows.anchor: أراد بالأول بيان حالهم في استحقاق عذاب الآخرة وفي الثاني بيان استحقاقهم لعذاب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation compares them first with Pharaoh’s people in denial and then in annihilation.
rows.anchor: إن في الأول تشبيه حالهم بحال أولئك في التكذيب وفي الثاني تشبيه حالهم بحالهم في الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says the first comparison concerns being seized by punishment and the second concerns its manner.
rows.anchor: إن الأول في أخذهم بالعذاب والثاني في كيفية العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Pharaoh’s people committed varied forms of disobedience, and the repetition shows these people shared those forms.
rows.anchor: إن آل فرعون كانوا على أحوال مختلفة في المعصية فبين مشاركة هؤلاء إياهم في تلك الأحوال

rows.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ḥamza and Yaʿqūb read the preceding question with tāʾ, addressing the believers; the other reading uses yāʾ as a rebuke to hypocrites.
rows.anchor: قرأ أولا ترون بالتاء حمزة ويعقوب وهي قراءة أبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن علية وابن محيصن والزهري
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUlayya, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and al-Zuhrī read min anfusikum with fatḥa, meaning from your noblest or best.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن علية وابن محيصن والزهري من أنفسكم بفتح الفاء

rows.speaker: فاطمة
rows.claim: The source also attributes the fatḥa reading of min anfusikum to Fāṭima.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنها قراءة فاطمة " ع ".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ reading addresses believers, while the yāʾ reading reproaches hypocrites for ignoring repentance and abandoning hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بالتاء فهو خطاب للمؤمنين ومن قرأ بالياء فهو تقريع للمنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, min anfusikum means from among your most noble and finest; anfus can mean the best of a thing because the soul is the finest part of a person.
rows.anchor: فمعناه من أشرفكم ومن خياركم يقال هذا أنفس المتاع أي أجوده وخياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzīz means powerful or difficult to overcome; as a divine attribute it means invincible and able to do whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: العزيز الشديد والعزيز في صفات الله تعالى معناه المنيع القادر الذي لا يتعذر عليه فعل ما يريده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIzza can mean invulnerability through power, scarcity, or difficulty.
rows.anchor: والعزة امتناع الشيء بما يتعذر معه ما يحاول منه وهو على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAnat is distress or harm that constricts the chest; its root also describes a broken animal leg that prevents running and a difficult ascent.
rows.anchor: والعنت لقاء الشدة والأذى الذي يضيق به الصدر وعنت الدابة يعنت عنتا إذا حدث في قوائمه كسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasbī Allāh means God is sufficient; the sense relates to accounting by sufficiency, with His gifts exceeding any limit.
rows.anchor: وحسبي الله أي كافي الله وهو من الحساب لأنه تعالى يعطي بحسب الكفاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reliance on God means entrusting one’s affairs to Him in confidence in His good direction and sufficiency.
rows.anchor: والتوكل تفويض الأمر إلى الله على الثقة بحسن تدبيره وكفايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a grammatical analysis, the waw is joined to the hamza of interrogation; yaraw may be a two-object verb or visual perception.
rows.anchor: الواو للعطف دخلت عليها همزة الاستفهام ويحتمل الرؤية أن تكون المتعدية إلى مفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ʿazīz ʿalayhi mā ʿanittum, mā is a verbal noun, so the sense is that your distress is hard on him and is nominative with ʿazīz.
rows.anchor: ما مصدرية وتقديره عزيز عليه عنتكم فهو في موضع رفع بعزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā ilāha illā huwa is a circumstantial clause, meaning God is sufficient while deserving exclusive worship and affirmation of unity.
rows.anchor: لا إله إلا هو جملة في موضع الحال وتقديره حسبي الله مستحقا لإخلاص العبادة والإقرار بالوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All canonical readers put al-ʿaẓīm in the accusative as an adjective of the Throne; nominative agreement with Lord would also be grammatically valid.
rows.anchor: ولو قرئ بالرفع على أن يكون صفة لرب العرش لجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebukes hypocrites for failing to reflect on their yearly trials; it says they are tested once or twice a year by illnesses and pains that herald death.
rows.anchor: أي أولا يعلم هؤلاء المنافقون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan interpret the yearly test as jihad with the Messenger and witnessing God’s support and the enemy’s deaths and captivity.
rows.anchor: يمتحنون بالجهاد مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما يرون من نصرة الله رسوله وما ينال أعداؤه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the trial consists of drought and hunger.
rows.anchor: بالقحط والجوع عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil interprets the trial as exposure of their secrets and the revelation of their corrupt inner state.
rows.anchor: بهتك استارهم وما يظهر من خبث سرائرهم عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk adds affliction, exile, withheld rain, and loss of crops as interpretations of the yearly trials.
rows.anchor: بالبلاء والجلاء ومنع القطر وذهاب الثمار عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a sūra is revealed in the Prophet’s presence, hypocrites exchange glances because they dislike its message and fear exposure, then leave.
rows.anchor: كرهوا ما يسمعونه ونظر بعضهم إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes their glances as a silent signal asking one another whether anyone is watching before they slip away.
rows.anchor: وإنما يفعلون ذلك مخافة أن تنزل آية تفضحهم وكانوا لا يقولون ذلك بألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says they look with derision at the Qur’an, checking whether any Muslim can see; if seen, they stop criticizing.
rows.anchor: نظر تعنت وطعن في القرآن ثم يقولون هل يرانا أحد من المسلمين فإذا تحقق لهم أنه لا يراهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then they turn away either by leaving the gathering or by turning away from faith.
rows.anchor: أي انصرفوا عن المجلس. وقيل: انصرفوا عن الإيمان به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s turning their hearts means depriving them of the benefit and joy that believers gain from revelation.
rows.anchor: عن الفوائد التي يستفيدها المؤمنون والسرور بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their hearts are turned from mercy and reward as punishment for turning away from faith, the Qur’an, and the Prophet’s gathering.
rows.anchor: صرف الله قلوبهم عن رحمته وثوابه عقوبة لهم على انصرافهم عن الإيمان بالقرآن

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim reads the phrase as a supplication against them: God abandons them because they deserve it, warning of the punishment that will overtake them.
rows.anchor: إنه على وجه الدعاء عليهم أي خذلهم الله باستحقاقهم ذلك ودعاء الله على عباده وعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fail to understand God’s intent in His address because they do not reflect on it.
rows.anchor: بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون } أي ذلك بسبب أنهم لا يفقهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is sworn and identifies the Messenger as Muḥammad, a human from the addressees’ own kind, then from the Arabs and descendants of Ismāʿīl.
rows.anchor: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم } عنى بالرسول محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains that Muḥammad was from the addressees’ own human kind, Arab people, and descendants of Ismāʿīl.
rows.anchor: من جنسكم من البشر ثم من العرب ثم من بني إسماعيل عن السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the address is to the Arabs and every Arab tribe had the Prophet’s lineage among it.
rows.anchor: إن الخطاب للعرب وليس في العرب قبيلة إلا وقد ولدت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وله فيهم نسب عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says Muḥammad descended only from lawful marriages and no illicit union in the pre-Islamic period.
rows.anchor: من نكاح لم يصبه شيء من ولادة الجاهلية عن الصادق ع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet saying that no fornication of the pre-Islamic period produced him; he descended only from marriages like those of Islam.
rows.anchor: ما ولدني من سفاح أهل الجاهلية شيء ما ولدني إلا نكاح كنكاح الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s people knew his origins and life from childhood to adulthood, and had seen his honesty and trustworthiness, so they had greater reason to accept and follow him.
rows.anchor: عرفوا مولده ومنشأه وشاهدوه صغيرا وكبيرا وعرفوا حاله في صدقه وأمانته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzīz ʿalayhi mā ʿanittum means that the harm you suffer by not believing is painful to him.
rows.anchor: معناه شديد عليه عنتكم أي ما يلحقكم من الضرر بترك الإيمان

rows.speaker: الكلبي والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain the phrase as the sins you commit being painful to him.
rows.anchor: شديد عليه ما أثمتم عن الكلبي والضحاك

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī interprets it as whatever causes you hardship and harm.
rows.anchor: ما أعنتكم وضركم عن القتيبي

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī takes it to mean the destruction you would suffer.
rows.anchor: ما هلكتم عليه عن ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say the Messenger is eager for unbelievers to come to faith.
rows.anchor: حريص على من لم يؤمن أن يؤمن عن الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats raʾūf and raḥīm as synonymous, with raʾfa denoting especially intense mercy.
rows.anchor: قيل: هما واحد والرأفة شدة الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations distinguish him as tender toward obedient believers and merciful toward sinners, toward kin and protégés, or toward those who see him and those who do not.
rows.anchor: وقيل: { رؤوف } بالمطيعين منهم { رحيم } بالمذنبين

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities say God combined two of His names for no prophet but Muḥammad, using this verse’s raʾūf and raḥīm; the same pair appears of God toward people.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض السلف لم يجمع الله سبحانه لأحد من الأنبياء بين اسمين من أسمائه إلا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away, they have left truth and the Messenger’s guidance and commands; another view says they turn away from him and deny his prophethood.
rows.anchor: { فإن تولوا } أي ذهبوا عن الحق واتباع الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasbī Allāh means God is sufficient; tawakkaltu means trusting and relying on Him and entrusting all affairs to Him.
rows.anchor: { فقل حسبي الله } أي كافي الله فإنه القادر على كل شيء

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says the Throne represents dominion and sovereignty, so Lord of the Great Throne means Lord of the great dominion in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: إن العرش عبارة عن الملك والسلطان فمعناه رب الملك العظيم في السماوات والأرض عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the Throne magnifies its status; if God is Lord of the immense Throne, He is Lord of everything below it.
rows.anchor: خص العرش بالذكر تفخيما لشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says these were the last verses revealed and al-Tawba was the last complete sūra; Qatāda says the two verses were the Qur’an’s last close contact with heaven.
rows.anchor: إن هذه الآية آخر آية نزلت من السماء وآخر سورة كاملة نزلت سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited expression from Maryam, under her means in front of her, since she was sitting above the stream rather than beneath it.
rows.anchor: لم يجعل السري الذي هو الجدول تحتها وهي قاعدة عليه وإنما أراد أنه جعله بين يديها

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī offers another reading: the rivers are beneath the people’s gardens, beds, and palaces.
rows.anchor: من تحت بساتينهم وأسرتهم وقصورهم عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By their faith means as recompense for their faith.
rows.anchor: يعني به جزاء على إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise invoke God with glorification, not as worship under a duty, but because they delight in praising Him.
rows.anchor: يقولون ذلك لا على وجه العبادة لأنه ليس هناك تكليف بل يلتذون بالتسبيح

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that a desired bird appears roasted when the people of Paradise glorify God, then returns alive after they praise God; glorification opens their speech and praise closes it.
rows.anchor: إذا مر بهم الطير في الهواء يشتهونه قالوا سبحانك اللهم فيأتيهم الطير فيقع مشويا بين أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Paradise, greeting with peace may come from God, from one another, or from angels, and means safety from the harms and trials of Hell’s inhabitants.
rows.anchor: تحيتهم من الله سبحانه في الجنة

rows.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Jubbāʾī say the praise at the end is not their final speech forever; it closes each thing they say.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد أن ذلك يكون آخر كلامهم حتى لا يتكلموا بعده بشئ

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads min kullin with tanwīn, while the other readers construct it with the following noun; the same difference occurs in al-Muʾminūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم { من كل زوجين } منونا

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
rows.claim: The Kūfan readers except Abū Bakr read majrāhā with fatḥa on the mīm; the others use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر مجريها بفتح الميم والباقون بضم الميم

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: All agree on ḍamma in mursal, apart from an anomalous report from Ibn Muḥayṣin opening the mīm in both words.
rows.anchor: واتفقوا على ضم الميم في مرسيها إلا ما يرى في الشواذ عن ابن محيصن أنه فتح الميم فيهما

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads yā bunayya irkab with fatḥa on the yāʾ, while the others read it with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم { يا بني اركب معنا } بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: علي وأبو جعفر وجعفر بن محمد وعروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: ʿAlī, Abū Jaʿfar, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, and ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr are reported to read the preceding phrase as Noḥ called his son.
rows.anchor: روي عن علي بن أبي طالب ع وأبي جعفر محمد بن علي وجعفر بن محمد عليهم السلام وعروة بن الزبير ونادى نوح ابنه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima is reported to read the word as his daughter.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عكرمة ابنها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī is reported to read it as his two sons.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي ابناه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to read son, pausing on it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ابنه على الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The justification for Ḥafṣ is that two are a pair, as in the verse saying God created everything in pairs; each spouse is also called the other’s pair.
rows.anchor: إن الاثنين زوجان قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s verse attests that zawj can refer to a pair or two associated things.
rows.anchor: من كل محفوف يظل عصيه زوج عليه كلة وقرامها

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With the genitive construction, ithnayn is the object of carry, and zawjayn means pairs as a generic class, not something short of three.
rows.anchor: كان قوله { اثنين } مفعول الحمل والمعنى

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s line supports using a pair expression to mean members of a larger group arranged two at a time.
rows.anchor: فاعمد لما يعلو فما لك بالذي لا تستطيع من الأمور يدان

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line likewise uses companions in pairs to refer to companions generally.
rows.anchor: وكل رفيقي كل رحل وإن هما تعاطى القنا قوما هما أخوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With tanwīn, the construction omits the genitive complement after kull and means from every thing and every kind, in pairs of two.
rows.anchor: فحذف المضاف إليه من كل ونون فالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a pair already implies two, ithnayn reinforces the meaning; the Qur’an similarly says two gods and uses other emphatic descriptions.
rows.anchor: فإنما جاز ذلك للتأكيد والتشديد كما قال:

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says bismi Allāh majrāhā can be a circumstantial phrase attached either to the pronoun in ride or to the pronoun in it, depending on the syntax.
rows.anchor: في قوله: { بسم الله مجراها ومرساها } أن يكون حالا من شيئين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: If bismi Allāh is a fronted predicate or majrāhā is raised by the adverb, the phrase can only describe the pronoun in it, since it has no reference back to the pronoun in ride.
rows.anchor: لم يكن { بسم الله مجراها } إلا جملة في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Under another parse, bismi Allāh describes those commanded to ride, as in riding equipped with weapons or clothed; they ride invoking and relying on God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بسم الله حالا من الضمير الذي في قوله { اركبوا }

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: On that parse, majrāhā attaches to the verbal sense of bismi Allāh and marks the times of running and anchoring; it does not modify ride, since they are not told to board at those times.
rows.anchor: وجاز تعلقه به لأن يكون ظرفا على نحو مقدم الحاج وخفوق النجم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Majrāhā is accusative as an adverb in the latter analysis, and nominative through an initial subject or adverb in the first.
rows.anchor: فموضع مجريها نصب على هذا الوجه بأنه ظرف عمل فيه المعنى وفي الوجه الأول رفع بالابتداء أو بالظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaddamtu al-qawm means walking ahead of a people so that they follow; the root and its forms also mean to go ahead or advance.
rows.anchor: قدمت القوم أقدمهم قدما إذا مشيت أمامهم واتبعوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ward can mean going to water or the incoming camels; irād is making something arrive at water or its equivalent, and ward originally means approaching entry rather than entering.
rows.anchor: والورد ورود الماء الذي يورد والإبل الواردة والجمع أوراد الإيراد إيجاب الورود في الماء

rows.speaker: الشاعر ولبيد وعنترة
rows.claim: Poetry by an unnamed poet, Labīd, and ʿAntara supplies examples of ward as arriving at or approaching water.
rows.anchor: وأصل الورود الاشراف على الدخول وليس بالدخول

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Rifd means support or help; al-Zajjāj says anything made an aid or support is rifd, and the word also means a gift because it helps its giver.
rows.anchor: كل شيء جعلته عونا لشيء أو اسندت به شيئا فقد رفدته به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣīd means harvested or cut from the root; it also describes people cut down by the sword.
rows.anchor: والحصيد بمعنى المحصود والحصد قطع الزرع من الأصل وهذا زمن الحصاد

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr’s verse uses tatbīb to mean ruin or loss.
rows.anchor: ألا تبا لما فعلوا تبابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdhāb differs from pain in being pain that continues.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين العذاب والألم أن العذاب استمرار الألم

rows.speaker: عبيد
rows.claim: ʿUbayd’s verse illustrates life spent in denial as a long punishment.
rows.anchor: والمرء ما عاش في تكذيب طول الحياة له تعذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Moses with signs proving his prophethood and with clear authority, an evident proof free from confusion or deception.
rows.anchor: بحججنا ومعجزاتنا الدالة على نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although signs and authority both mean proofs, signs are proofs by their great evidentiary force and authority is proof by its power to defeat false argument.
rows.anchor: الآيات حجج من وجه الاعتبار العظيم بها والسلطان حجة من جهة القوة العظيمة على المبطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the authority of proof exceeds the authority of rule; a truthful authority must be followed, while an untruthful one need not be.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن سلطان الحجة أنفذ من سلطان المملكة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says sultān is God’s proof on earth, deriving it from salīṭ, the lamp by which one sees.
rows.anchor: السلطان إنما سمي سلطانا لأنه حجة الله في أرضه واشتقاقه من السليط الذي يستضاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s people means his subjects; another view means the prominent leaders whose presence fills hearts with awe.
rows.anchor: أشراف قومه الذين تملأ الصدور هيبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They followed Pharaoh’s command and abandoned God’s; Pharaoh’s command was not a guide to right or good but called to evil and blocked good.
rows.anchor: ما هو بهاد لهم إلى رشد ولا قائد إلى خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here amr can refer to either speech or deed; the author takes it to mean what Pharaoh did.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن لفظة الأمر مشتركة بين القول والفعل والمراد ها هنا وما فعل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day of Resurrection Pharaoh walks before his people on foot and leads them into Fire, as he led them in this life toward its path.
rows.anchor: يعني أن فرعون يمشي بين يدي قومه يوم القيامة على قدميه حتى يهجم بهم على النار

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says fa-awradahum uses past form for a future event because the preceding phrase places it on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: على لفظ الماضي والمراد به المستقبل لأن ما عطفه عليه من قوله يقدم قومه يوم القيامة يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis coordinates fa-awradahum with the past statement that they followed Pharaoh’s command.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه معطوف على قوله { فاتبعوا أمر فرعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is the worst watering place: they arrive thirsty seeking life, but find Fire; calling it ward contrasts with Paradise’s rivers and springs.
rows.anchor: بئس الماء الذي يردونه عطاشا لإحياء نفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations call it the worst entrance, the worst thing they are brought to, or the worst allotted share.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه بئس المدخل المدخول فيه النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word biʾsa is appropriate even though God’s justice is good, because the outcome is misery and severity.
rows.anchor: وإنما أطلق بلفظ بئس وإن كان عدلا حسنا لما فيه من البؤس والشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse that follows Pharaoh’s people in this world is drowning, and the curse of the Resurrection is the punishment of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني ألحقوا في الدنيا { لعنة } وهي الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God banished them from mercy in this life, the prophets and believers cursed them, and the curse will follow them at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه اتبعهم الله في الدنيا لعنة بإبعادهم من الرحمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that anyone who mentions Pharaoh’s people curses them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس من ذكرهم لعنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire and curse are a terrible gift, called a gift in contrast to the blessings given to Paradise’s people.
rows.anchor: بئس العطاء المعطي النار واللعنة وإنما سماه رفدا لأنه في مقابلة ما يعطى أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says two curses from God befell them, one in this life and one in the next.
rows.anchor: ترافدت عليهم لعنتان من الله لعنة في الدنيا ولعنة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked by Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq about the worst gift, Ibn ʿAbbās answered that it is curse upon curse.
rows.anchor: وسأل نافع بن الأزرق ابن عباس عن قوله { بئس الرفد المرفود } قال: هو اللعنة بعد اللعنة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the two curses each supported the other.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: اللعنتان اللتان أصابتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is news of earlier towns that God relates to Muḥammad as a reminder and consolation; some remain standing, others were destroyed.
rows.anchor: أن نذكره لك ونخبرك به تذكرة وتسلية لك يا محمد

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Qatāda and Abū Muslim interpret standing towns as structures still standing though abandoned, and harvested towns as ruined and erased.
rows.anchor: منها قائم على بنائه لم يذهب أصلا وإن كان خاليا من أهله وحصيد قد خرب وذهب واندرس أثره كالشيء المحصود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the standing towns are those people look upon, while the harvested ones have perished along with their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: منها قائم ينظرون إليها وحصيد قد هلك وباد أهله عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not wrong the people by destroying them; they wronged themselves through disbelief and actions that made them deserve destruction.
rows.anchor: بأن كفروا وارتكبوا ما استحقوا به الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their idols could not help when God’s punishment or decree of destruction arrived.
rows.anchor: أي أوثانهم { التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda gloss tatbīb as loss and destruction: the idols increased nothing but ruin.
rows.anchor: أي غير تخسير عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols are described as causing the ruin because idol worship was its cause; they called them gods and sought needs from them as monotheists seek from God.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضاف الإهلاك إلى الأصنام لأنها السبب في ذلك ولو لم يعبدوها لم يهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s seizure of towns repeats the pattern of earlier nations’ destruction; taking towns means taking their residents into punishment and ruin.
rows.anchor: إذا أخذ القرى } أي أخذ أهلها وهو أن ينقلهم
